title: The Semester of the quarry
premise: Felix Montrose, the only out kid in the quarry town of Harrow Bend, keeps her head down until she finds her late grandmother's recipe box hiding spell-directions instead of recipes. The magic is tied to the quarry itself, and the town's most powerful family has been quietly draining its memory-stone for generations to keep their grip on Harrow Bend. As Felix learns the craft, she discovers her best friend Priya's family is one of the beneficiaries, and exposing the truth will cost her the friendship she can't survive senior year without. Felix chooses truth over safety, breaks the quarry's hold, and ends the semester with a smaller life but an honest one — grieving the friendship, but finally visible.
about_author: Odile Nystrom grew up in a small mining town where everyone knew everyone's business and no one said anything out loud. She writes YA fiction about queer kids who refuse to stay quiet, and still keeps her grandmother's recipe box on her desk.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ash
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Sorting her grandmother's belongings after the funeral, Felix finds a recipe card for 'Remembering Bread' whose instructions are clearly not for baking. She dismisses it as grief-brain, but copies it into her notebook anyway. Beat: loneliness sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: The Nine Hundred
chapters.summary: POV Felix. First week of senior semester; Felix navigates being the only out kid in Harrow Bend, leaning on her best friend Priya Chaudhary, whose family owns half the quarry leases. A card slips from Felix's locker — someone knows about the box. Beat: the comfort of routine, cracked.

chapters.title: Remembering Bread
chapters.summary: POV Felix. On a dare to herself, Felix follows the card exactly in her kitchen. The loaf comes out gray and warm, and eating it floods her with her grandmother's memory of the quarry the day the Montrose family lost their claim. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: What Grandma Knew
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix tests the craft: a card for 'Clear Water,' one for 'Steady Hands.' Each works, and each draws something from her — color, sleep, words. She realizes the recipes trade memory for power. Beat: hungry, frightened competence.

chapters.title: The Vane Family
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Researching the lost claim, Felix learns the Vane family took the Montrose quarry in 1961 and has run the town since. Mayor Elias Vane smiles at her at the diner and knows her name. Beat: the sense of being watched.

chapters.title: Priya's Secret
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya sees Felix slipping notes from a recipe box and assumes Felix is hiding a relationship or a crisis. She covers for Felix at school without being asked, deepening their bond — and Priya's own secret: her father is the Vanes' quarry foreman. Beat: loyalty with a hairline fracture.

chapters.title: The Stone That Listens
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix sneaks into the quarry at night with a 'Finding' card and touches the exposed seam of memory-stone. It shows her generations of borrowed memories — including her grandmother's, stored there against her will. Beat: righteous fury.

chapters.title: Small Town Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix maps who benefits: the Vanes, the school board, the sheriff. Every 'lucky' family in Harrow Bend has a recipe card somewhere. She starts photographing the box's contents. Beat: the planner's cold clarity.

chapters.title: Detention with Mr. Vane
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Elias Vane's son, Theo, catches Felix in the school archive and instead of reporting her, asks what she found. He's been having memories that aren't his. Beat: an unexpected ally, distrusted.

chapters.title: The First Cost
chapters.summary: POV Felix. To prove the stone's theft to Theo, Felix bakes a 'Returning' card — and loses her clearest memory of her mother's face. Grief and power in the same mouthful. Beat: the theme made flesh; power always bills you.

chapters.title: Priya Asks Questions
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya notices Felix's memory lapses and confronts her. Felix lies — the first real lie between them — and Priya knows it. Beat: the friendship's first true wound, self-inflicted.

chapters.title: The Foreman's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Torn, Priya copies pages from her father's quarry ledger: decades of 'tonnage' that is actually harvested memory, sold upstate. She doesn't tell Felix she has it. Beat: complicity versus conscience.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The Vanes, alerted by Theo's snooping, escalate — Felix's locker is emptied, her grandmother's house is 'assessed' for back taxes. A warning card appears in her mailbox, written in her grandmother's handwriting. Beat: fear closing in.

chapters.title: What the Stone Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix and Theo return to the seam and find her grandmother's stored memories intact — including the recipe for unmaking the quarry's hold. It requires a memory freely given, not taken. Beat: hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Elias Vane offers Felix her family's claim back, her college fund, silence about her — if she hands over the box and stops digging. He is kind, which is worse. Beat: temptation, and the taste of corruption.

chapters.title: The Falling Out
chapters.summary: POV Priya. Priya's father is fired for the missing ledger pages; the family's livelihood is now hostage to Felix's crusade. Priya tells Felix to stop, and Felix says the truth out loud about what Priya's family took. Beat: the friendship breaks — loudly, in the school parking lot.

chapters.title: Alone, Out Loud
chapters.summary: POV Felix. With Priya gone and graduation weeks away, Felix considers taking the Vane offer. She spends a day being invisible and safe and can't stand it. She writes the truth on the diner's specials board. Beat: choosing visibility at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Half of Harrow Bend reads the board; the other half burns Felix's porch steps. Theo publicly backs her, splitting the Vane name. Elias moves to seize the recipe box through the sheriff. Beat: the town itself becomes a character, waking.

chapters.title: Quarry Night
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix, Theo, and a hesitating Priya break into the quarry to bake the unmaking at the seam. Elias and the foremen confront them. Priya steps between Felix and her father — and hands Felix the ledger. Beat: climax begins; loyalty re-forged in the open.

chapters.title: Freely Given
chapters.summary: POV Felix. To fuel the unmaking, Felix offers her happiest memory — the day Priya stood up for her in ninth grade — freely, without knowing what it will cost. The stone releases everything it holds over Harrow Bend. Beat: the climax's peak; power undone by gift.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: POV Priya. The quarry goes quiet; the Vanes' leverage dissolves; investigations begin. Priya's family loses everything but each other. She and Felix stand at the fence line, not friends yet, but no longer enemies. Beat: grief and respect, side by side.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: POV Felix. At graduation, Felix — out, unhidden, her memory of Priya's kindness gone but a new one beginning — receives her diploma to mixed applause. In her pocket: a blank recipe card, and her grandmother's last note: 'Write your own.' Beat: resolution; inheritance reclaimed as choice.
